A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SKCI research work. All 25 pages, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C, were readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Gaussian and CI-hardness data, simulated neural activity, dSprites and car-insurance data, including supplementary experiments and ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix C, including Type I error, power, long-horizon and ablation results.

M1.justification: The SKCI procedure, normalization, shift-and-truncate calibration and optimization remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. Rewriting g(t)(yj) as a function g(t)(y) clarifies notation without changing its computation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian, CI-hardness, RatInABox, dSprites and car-insurance tasks, with the same applicable Oracle, Pretrained and Online scenarios.

E2.justification: e-CRT, DAVT and EC2ST remain the comparators in the corresponding experiments. Their participation in Figures 1–10 and their configurations in Appendix B.4 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same protocols, including default batch size 20, 3,000 auxiliary samples for Pretrained mode, baseline tuning procedures, architectures and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains identical long-horizon null experiments and ablations of batch size, denominator regularization and conservative shift perturbation. Figures 11–12 and their accompanying analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 independent runs by default, 50 runs per state/company pair for car insurance, and standard-error shading. Seed information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–12 retain identical plotted results, and the corresponding findings in Section 5 and Appendix C are unchanged. No result entries, numerical outcomes or reported rankings were added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: Section 2.3, footnote 1 withdraws v1's assertion that Györfi and Walk's test establishes distribution-free strong consistency. v2 reports an incorrect proof and treats existence of such control as open, with a cited partial negative result. SKCI's own lemmas, theorems and Appendix A proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same contributions and claims about adaptive betting, robustness to conditional-distribution estimation error, and Type I error versus power. The background correction does not redefine SKCI's central claims.

C2.justification: The revised footnote distinguishes what impossibility results leave open from what has actually been established: non-uniform asymptotic control is no longer presented as an available guarantee. Interpretations of SKCI's results and its finite-horizon limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B's preprocessing, kernel choices, model configurations and hyperparameters are identical. Code and data access information is retained; the main-text notation clarification supplies no new implementation setting.

R1.justification: v2 adds Neykov et al. (2021) and Boeken et al. (2026) to qualify the discussion of strong consistency and impossibility. This is a limited correction to the account of prior theory, without a broader change in research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the filtration as a sigma-algebra, rewrites the introduction of g(t), revises footnote 1 and updates citation wording and acknowledgements. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The edits cause limited text and equation reflow across pages 3–6 and in the bibliography. Figures 1–12, Tables 1–4 and the algorithm display retain their content and overall arrangement.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces an unqualified strong-consistency assertion with an explicit account of a reported proof flaw and the remaining open question in Section 2.3, footnote 1. Together with clearer filtration and payoff notation, this improves precision. The method, original proofs and empirical evidence remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
